title: Affine module correspondence on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:Y\to X$ be an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning representable with affine scheme base changes. Use the small etale structure sheaves, module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], tensor pullback and module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Put $\mathcal A=p_*\mathcal O_Y$, a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra. For any sheaf $M$ of $\mathcal A$-modules, being quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module (etale locally admitting a presentation by sums of $\mathcal A$) is equivalent to its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module being quasi-coherent. Direct image, with its natural $\mathcal A$-action, induces an additive equivalence from $\operatorname{QCoh}(Y)$ to the category of these quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-modules, whose morphisms are $\mathcal A$-linear module maps. This equivalence is compatible with etale base change on $X$. Explicitly, for an affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, put $C=\mathcal A(U)$; then $Y_U=Y\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and the inverse equivalence sends $M$ to the module whose restriction to $Y_U$ is the etale module associated to the $C$-module $M(U)$. On these charts morphisms are the corresponding $C$-linear maps, and the free module $\mathcal A^{\oplus n}$ corresponds to $\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus n}$ for each finite $n$.

source.place: Tag 08AI, lemma-affine-equivalence-modules; the affine chart description and etale compatibility spell out its equivalence using the affine algebra correspondence Tag 081V (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras).

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=p_*\mathcal O_Y$. The relative-spectrum correspondence says that $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent and that, for an affine etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, $Y_U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C=\mathcal A(U)$. Its base-change clause identifies $C'=\mathcal A(U')$ with $C\otimes_RR'$ whenever $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\to U$ is a morphism of affine etale charts. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U_0\to X$ which is a disjoint union of affines. Then $V_0=Y\times_XU_0\to Y$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas, again a disjoint union of affines. Scheme representability follows from the assumed affineness of $p$.

Suppose $M$ is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module. On an etale cover take a presentation $\mathcal A^{(I)}\to\mathcal A^{(J)}\to M\to0$. Forgetting the action gives the same cokernel presentation of $\mathcal O$-modules. Since $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent, its direct sums and this cokernel are quasi-coherent by the kernels-and-colimits lemma. Quasi-coherence is local by its presentation definition, so the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent. No finiteness condition on $I,J$ is used.

Conversely suppose the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module of $M$ is quasi-coherent. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ put $N=M(U)$. The chart correspondence identifies $\mathcal A|_U$ with $\widetilde C$ and $M|_U$ with $\widetilde N$ on the etale site. The action gives a $C$-module structure on $N$. It recovers the sheaf action: the tensor chart formula identifies its source with the associated sheaf of $C\otimes_RN$, and the tilde--sections bijection, transported through the scheme etale/Zariski equivalence, identifies the action map with $c\otimes n\mapsto cn$. Choose a free $C$-module presentation $C^{(I)}\to C^{(J)}\to N\to0$. The chart correspondence computes coproducts and cokernels, so the associated sequence is an exact presentation $\mathcal A|_U^{(I)}\to\mathcal A|_U^{(J)}\to M|_U\to0$. Its maps are $\mathcal A$-linear because their $C$-linear section maps commute with the action, and the same tilde--sections bijection detects that equality. This proves quasi-coherence over $\mathcal A$ on a cover, hence globally.

source.place: Tag 03LZ (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale), Tag 03M1; morphisms.tex Tag 0H88, converse proof; schemes.tex Tags 01I7, 01IB; descent.tex Tag 03DX.

proof.text: For $F\in\operatorname{QCoh}(Y)$ and an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$, let $P=F(Y_U)$, a module over $C=\mathcal A(U)$. Direct-image restriction identifies $(p_*F)|_U$ with the direct image from $Y_U$. On an affine etale $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\to U$, its sections are $F(Y_{U'})=P\otimes_C(C\otimes_RR')$, by affine pullback sections and the scheme etale/Zariski pullback comparison. The isomorphism to $P\otimes_RR'$ sends $p\otimes(c\otimes r')$ to $cp\otimes r'$; its inverse sends $p\otimes r'$ to $p\otimes(1\otimes r')$. These formulas commute with further restrictions. Thus $(p_*F)|_U$ is the etale associated sheaf of the underlying $R$-module $P$, with the $\widetilde C$-action induced by its $C$-action. Affine etale objects cover every object of $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, so the section comparisons identify the sheaves. Consequently $p_*F$ is quasi-coherent over $\mathcal O_X$, hence over $\mathcal A$ by step 3. Module maps push forward to $\mathcal A$-linear maps.

For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module $M$, set $N_U=M(U)$ and on $Y_U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ take the etale associated sheaf $H_U=\widetilde{N_U}$ over $C$. If $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\to U$, put $C'=C\otimes_RR'$. The underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent by step 2, so the affine pullback formula identifies $N_{U'}$ with $N_U\otimes_RR'$. Under this identification $C'$ acts by $(c\otimes r')(n\otimes s')=cn\otimes r's'$; this follows by restricting the original action map. Therefore the map $N_U\otimes_CC'\to N_{U'}$, $n\otimes(c\otimes r')\mapsto cn\otimes r'$, is an isomorphism, with inverse $n\otimes r'\mapsto n\otimes(1\otimes r')$. The affine pullback formula identifies it with a pullback isomorphism $H_U|_{Y_{U'}}\simeq H_{U'}$. For two successive chart maps both composite isomorphisms send a pure tensor to the product of its scalars acting on $n$. Hence they agree; the identity chart map gives the identity. The construction commutes with every $C$-linear map of sections.

source.place: Tag 03LZ; schemes.tex Tag 01I9; descent.tex Tag 03LC. Explicit chart calculation supplying the omitted proof of spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 08AI.

proof.text: Use the atlas $V_0\to Y$ from step 1. On its affine components take the modules $H_U$ of step 5, viewed as Zariski modules through the scheme etale/Zariski equivalence. The overlap is $V_0\times_YV_0=Y\times_X(U_0\times_XU_0)$. Cover the scheme $U_0\times_XU_0$ by affine opens, refining into the affine components of both projections to $U_0$. Step 5 identifies the two pullbacks of the local modules over each of these opens, using the common module of sections of $M$ on that chart of $X$. These identifications agree under refinement, so glue by the sheaf property. On a similarly refined triple overlap their cocycle is precisely the multiplication-of-scalars identity in step 5; along the diagonal it is the identity. The groupoid quasi-coherent equivalence now descends this datum to $H(M)\in\operatorname{QCoh}(Y)$. Compatible local maps descend uniquely, so $M\mapsto H(M)$ is a functor. The same overlap argument, comparing any additional affine chart with the atlas, identifies its restriction to $Y_U$ with $H_U$. The overlap schemes need not themselves be affine.

source.place: Tag 03M3 (proposition-quasi-coherent), descent for an etale scheme atlas; Tag 02X2 (spaces, lemma-fibre-product-spaces); descent.tex Tag 03LC.

proof.text: For each affine $U$, the sections of $p_*H(M)$ are the sections of $H_U$ on $\operatorname{Spec}C$, namely $N_U=M(U)$, by the tilde unit isomorphism. Step 5 makes these identities compatible with restrictions and with the $\mathcal A$-action, giving $p_*H(M)\simeq M$. Conversely, for $F\in\operatorname{QCoh}(Y)$, the restriction of $H(p_*F)$ to $Y_U$ is the associated sheaf of $F(Y_U)$; the tilde counit isomorphism identifies it with $F|_{Y_U}$. Naturality of the tilde unit and counit makes these maps agree on overlaps, and descent gives $H(p_*F)\simeq F$. The isomorphisms are natural in maps. An $\mathcal A$-linear map induces on $U$ exactly a $C$-linear map; the tilde--sections Hom bijection and descent give its unique corresponding map on $Y$. Composition, identities and addition are computed on those same section maps. Thus direct image and $H$ form the asserted additive equivalence with the specified morphisms.

source.place: Schemes, Tags 01I7, 01HV, 01IA, 01IB (tilde--sections unit, counit and Hom bijection); spaces-properties.tex Tags 03M3, 03LX.

proof.text: Let $g:X'\to X$ be etale and $Y'=Y\times_XX'$, with projection $p'$. The direct-image restriction theorem identifies $g^*(p_*F)$ with $p'_*(F|_{Y'})$ as the identity on compatible sections, and likewise identifies $g^*\mathcal A$ with $p'_*\mathcal O_{Y'}$. The identifications respect multiplication and module action since both are defined by the same products of restricted sections. For the inverse, every affine etale chart $T\to X'$ is also one of $X$; both constructions restrict on $Y'\times_{X'}T=Y\times_XT$ to the associated module of $M(T)$. The overlap maps are exactly those of step 5, so descent identifies the inverse functors and the unit and counit of step 7. For successive etale base changes these comparisons compose, because they are identities on the same compatible sections. This proves the claimed etale compatibility, including non-scheme $X'$.

source.place: Tag 03LX (lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules), with Tag 03M3 for descent of the inverse comparison.

proof.text: Finally, on an affine etale $U$, the module of sections of $\mathcal A^{\oplus n}$ is $C^{\oplus n}$. Its associated module on $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is $\mathcal O^{\oplus n}$, since tilde preserves these coproducts and sends $C$ to the structure module. The overlap identifications send each standard basis vector to the same standard basis vector. Hence these local identifications descend to $H(\mathcal A^{\oplus n})\simeq\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus n}$. This includes $n=0$.
